newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes quiet, but ANS deal gets done.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes quiet, but ANS deal gets done.

text.p: A mostly quiet U.S. West Coast crude market was stirred by an Alaskan North Slope (ANS) deal as West Texas Intermediate/Cushing rose a bit, players said.
The seller, British Petroleum said the cargo deal was done at $1.95 under January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, above the last deal at $2.20 under December WTI.

While the outright price of the deal could not be confirmed, the buyer of the 600,000 barrel cargo for delivery in Honolulu during December, Broken Hill Properties, said the deal was priced off December WTI plus the "roll," with the value of the latter pricing component not known.
Confirmation of the deal followed vague talk earlier that an ANS deal got done Tuesday at $2.20 under January WTI.
Traders said talk was otherwise rather light Tuesday, with liquidity hurt by the coming U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday, which was already pulling players out of the market.
Additionally, players said the West Coast crude market was generally sluggish amid a rather poor refinery profit margin outlook that kept many players rushing to close crude deals.
Still, Wilmington crude was notionally talked about five cents firmer at 55/60 cents over posted the posted average or at between $18.35/$18.45 a barrel, traders said.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
